settings.activityHelp: Checks whether Homey has seen the device recently.
settings.timestampHelp: Use this when the device or app keeps track of when new data was last received.
settings.manualHelp: Let a Homey Flow confirm after a successful update that everything is still working.
settings.timestampHint: Check the time field for each device. The value itself must show when new data was received.
settings.selectDevice: Select a device first. If it is missing, refresh the inventory.
settings.selectCapability: Select which timestamp indicates that new data has been received.
settings.timingOrder: Consider stale after must be equal to or longer than the expected update interval.
settings.observedMinimum: Activity and timestamp checks require a stale timeout of at least 2 minutes.
settings.invalidTiming: Enter a duration greater than zero, up to 525600 minutes (whole milliseconds).
settings.failed: The monitor could not be saved. Check the highlighted fields.
settings.retry: The monitor could not be saved. Try again; your changes are still here.
settings.missingField: Saved field is currently missing. The selection is preserved; check the source.
settings.duplicate: This device already has a monitor. Choose Edit in the list.
settings.chooseMethod: Choose how freshness should be checked.
settings.maxFields: Select no more than 16 timestamp fields.
settings.chooseEncoding: Select the timestamp format used by the source.
settings.noteLimit: Keep the technical note within 2000 characters.
settings.optionalNoteLimit: Keep the optional note within 2000 characters.
settings.duplicateRefresh: This device already has a monitor. Refresh and edit the existing monitor.
settings.identityChanged: This device no longer belongs to the selected integration. Refresh and check the device.
settings.monitorMissing: This monitor no longer exists. Cancel and refresh before trying again.
settings.savedRefreshFailed: Monitor saved. Status could not be refreshed; use Refresh to try again.
settings.refreshSuffix: Status could not be refreshed; use Refresh status to try again.
settings.emptyInventory: No devices are currently listed. Refresh the inventory to try again.
settings.timestampField: Which field contains the time data was received?
settings.noTimestampFields: This device has no suitable time field for ‘Last data received’. Choose Device activity or Flow confirmation.
settings.confirmBeforeSaving: Confirm or cancel the device selection before saving.
settings.maxMonitors: You can configure up to 500 monitors.
settings.missingDevice: __name__ is no longer in the inventory. Deselect it or refresh before saving.
settings.alreadyHasMonitor: __name__ already has a monitor. Deselect it and use Edit.
settings.refreshFailed: Could not refresh the status. Try again.
settings.loadFailed: Could not load settings. Use Refresh to retry.
settings.deviceHelp: Choose the device whose freshness you want to monitor.
settings.capabilitiesHelp: The field value itself must contain a date and time, not a measurement or its last-change time. With several fields, a new time in any one counts as an update. Check that the source updates it when data is received.
settings.emptyCapabilities: This device has no suitable time field for ‘Last data received’. Choose Device activity or Flow confirmation.
settings.encodingHelp: Match the format used by the source. The local test source uses ISO.
settings.expectedHelp: How often should this source normally report activity or data?
settings.timeoutHelp: Alert when no valid update has been seen for this long. Activity and timestamp checks require at least 2 minutes.
settings.contractHelp: Optional note about why this signal provides reliable evidence of activity or delivery. Editing this note does not restart monitoring.
settings.emptyMonitors: No monitors yet. Choose Add monitor to get started.
settings.updateFailed: Could not update __name__. Your previous settings are kept.
settings.activityDetail: This proves activity, not necessarily a new measurement or successful delivery.
settings.dataDetail: The selected field must itself contain a date/time value updated by the source. A measurement value or its lastUpdated metadata is not a substitute. If several fields are selected, a new time in any one counts as an update.
settings.flowDetail: The confirmation must follow a real successful update. A blind repeating timer does not prove that the source works. Existing API confirmations remain supported.
settings.helpTimingExample: For updates every 5 minutes, you might expect an update every 5 minutes and alert after 15 minutes. Allow some margin for delays. The timeout must be at least the expected interval. Device activity and Last data received require at least 2 minutes.
settings.helpFirstTest: For a first test, monitor the test device with Last data received, Last test heartbeat, ISO format, a 0.5-minute expected interval and a 2-minute timeout.
settings.helpMethodTrouble: If Last data received never becomes Healthy, check the selected field, format and whether its time moves forward. If Device activity stays Unknown, Homey may not provide a usable last-seen time.
settings.helpStart: Choose Add monitor above the list, then choose how to check for updates.
settings.helpSave: Choose Add monitors. Fields needing attention will be highlighted.
settings.unverifiedSavedField: Saved field: its current value was not recognized as a suitable time. Check the source; the selection is preserved.
settings.savedFormatMismatch: Saved field: its current value does not match the saved time format. Check the format; the selection is preserved.
settings.fieldFormatMismatch: The chosen time format does not match all selected fields. Choose fields with the same format.
settings.help_basics_1: Data Pulse checks whether a device or integration still shows valid activity or data delivery. It does not simply check whether a measurement changes: a temperature can stay at 21.3 °C while the sensor works perfectly.
settings.help_quick_start_1: Open Select devices, choose one or more sources, then confirm with Use selection.
settings.help_quick_start_2: Enter how often updates are normally expected.
settings.help_quick_start_3: Set the timing once for your selection. Open Adjust settings per device only when a source needs different timing.
settings.help_quick_start_4: For phone notifications, create a Homey Flow using Any watchdog incident started.
settings.help_timing_1: Expected update interval: how often should the source normally report activity or new data?
settings.help_timing_2: Consider stale after: how long may no valid update arrive before the source is treated as stale?
settings.help_timing_3: The input arrows move in half-minute steps: 0.5 is 30 seconds; 1.5 is 90 seconds. A short confirmation period means an incident notification may follow slightly after the timeout. Recovery also needs to remain stable before the incident closes.
settings.help_statuses_1: Waiting for a fresh update after setup, restart or a change to how freshness is checked.
settings.help_statuses_2: Recent valid activity or data delivery has been confirmed.
settings.help_statuses_3: The signal is overdue. Data Pulse waits briefly before declaring an incident.
settings.help_statuses_4: The device has missed the configured stale period and an incident is active. It may be grouped with other devices from the same integration.
settings.help_statuses_5: Fresh updates have returned; waiting for stable recovery before closing the incident.
settings.help_statuses_6: Monitoring is turned off for this monitor.
settings.help_statuses_7: The configured device or required timestamp field cannot currently be found.
settings.help_statuses_8: A reliable state cannot currently be determined, for example because observation is unavailable.
settings.help_notifications_1: Data Pulse detects incidents; it does not automatically send everyone a push notification. Create a Homey Flow to choose who receives messages and which incidents to report.
settings.help_notifications_2: WHEN: Data Pulse → Any watchdog incident started.
settings.help_notifications_3: THEN: Homey → Send a push notification. Choose the recipient and message.
settings.help_notifications_4: For an optional recovery message, create a second Flow using Any watchdog incident recovered. You can use the device and integration information supplied by the trigger in your message. Avoid sending the same notification from both a general incident trigger and a device-specific trigger.
settings.help_notifications_5: If several monitors from the same integration stop reporting together, Data Pulse can group them into one integration incident.
settings.help_self_test_1: Pair Data Pulse Test Source (simulation) only if you want a safe local test of stale detection, recovery and your notification Flows. It does not control production devices and is not needed for daily monitoring. Test incidents can send real notifications through your existing watchdog Flows.
settings.help_self_test_2: Start test: sends a confirmation now, then every 30 seconds.
settings.help_self_test_3: Stop: stops the heartbeat and freezes the test timestamp.
settings.help_self_test_4: Send once: sends one heartbeat without starting a stopped simulator. An already running simulator stays running.
settings.help_self_test_5: After an app restart, the test deliberately starts stopped.
settings.help_advanced_1: Edit changes the existing monitor; Save changes keeps it, while Cancel discards the draft. Changing the freshness method or timing starts a new observation period. Disable pauses monitoring.
settings.help_advanced_2: Technical note is optional. Use it to remember why you trust a freshness signal. It does not affect detection or restart monitoring.
settings.help_troubleshooting_0: If something does not look right
settings.help_troubleshooting_1: Use Refresh. If Starting persists, check that the chosen source is producing new updates. For Missing, check that the device and time field still exist. A normal rename alone does not remove a monitor.
settings.help_troubleshooting_2: If no phone notification arrives, check your incident Flow, its conditions, recipient and Homey push permissions.
settings.help_limitations_1: Monitoring is only as trustworthy as the selected freshness signal. A wrong time field can make an unhealthy source appear healthy. An unchanged measurement is not proof of a fault, and activity is not proof of new measurement data.
settings.help_limitations_2: If the whole Homey stops running, Data Pulse on that same Homey cannot report its own outage. Monitoring the entire host requires a separate solution outside that Homey; this app does not provide that external monitoring.
settings.testIntro: Local simulation only. Test incidents use your normal watchdog notification Flows. Production devices are not controlled.
settings.testUnpaired: Pair the optional Data Pulse Test Source device to safely test monitoring and notifications.
settings.testRestartHint: Starts stopped after every app restart. Stop freezes the time field; Send once leaves a stopped source stopped.
settings.metadataWarning: Some integration names or zones could not be loaded. Monitoring may still be available.
settings.testRefreshFailed: Could not refresh the local test source. Try again.
settings.testCommandFailed: The test command failed. Check the test source and try again.
settings.testSourceStopped: The test confirmation failed; the source has stopped.
settings.testNativeFailed: Homey activity could not be updated. The time field and Flow confirmations remain available.
settings.testSourceError: The local test source reported an error. See the details.
